Describe how something is made or done: coffee, bread, a passport, or something at your work. Use at least three passive sentences.
exercicios.frase: checked
exercicios.resposta: In my bank, a new account is opened in three steps. First, the documents are checked at the front desk. Then the client's information is entered in the system. After that, the card is sent to the branch, and the client is called. It usually takes a week.

exercicios.enunciado: Do you think solar energy is a good idea for Angola? Why?
exercicios.frase: think
exercicios.resposta: Yes, I think it's a very good idea. We have sun almost every day, and in many villages there's no electricity. In some villages, small solar panels are used in the schools, and the children can study at night.

Tell me the history of a building, a company or a project. Say when it was started, built or opened, and give two more facts. Use the passive.
exercicios.frase: opened
exercicios.resposta: My company was started in 2010 by two engineers from Benguela. The first office was opened in Lobito, and our head office was built in Luanda in 2019. Last year, a new branch was opened in Huambo, and twenty people were hired.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it better to hire local people for a big project, or experienced people from other places? Why?
exercicios.frase: hired
exercicios.resposta: In my view, it's better to hire local people, and train them. For example, at the plant in Namibe, most of the workers were hired in the region. The money stays there, and the people stay after the project.

Describe your workplace or your school to a new colleague: two people, one thing and one place. Use "who", "that" or "which", and "where".
exercicios.frase: where
exercicios.resposta: Ana is the person who answers the phone, and João is the manager who signs the contracts. The printer that works best is on the second floor. And the kitchen is the place where everyone meets at eleven for coffee.

exercicios.enunciado: What's the most important thing a new colleague needs to know on the first day? Why?
exercicios.frase: who
exercicios.resposta: In my opinion, a new colleague needs to know the people who can help. For example, the person who fixes the computers, and the colleague who knows all the procedures. Then the first week is much easier.

What are the safety rules at your work, or in a place you know? Say two things people must do, one thing they mustn't do, and one thing they don't have to do.
exercicios.frase: mustn't
exercicios.resposta: In the hospital where I work, you must wash your hands before you see a patient, and you have to wear your ID card all the time. You mustn't use your phone in the operating rooms. But visitors don't have to wear a uniform.

exercicios.enunciado: In your opinion, which energy is best for Angola in the future: oil, gas, or renewable energy? Why?
exercicios.frase: renewable
exercicios.resposta: In my view, renewable energy is the best, because the sun and the rivers don't run out. A lot of our electricity is already produced by dams. But oil is still important for the economy, so we need both for some years.

A colleague missed the tour. Explain how the satellite backup works, and two safety rules.
exercicios.frase: sent
exercicios.resposta: The data from the sensors is collected every minute and sent to the control room by the radio link. When the link goes down, the satellite starts working automatically. And two rules: you have to wear a helmet and a vest outside the offices, and you mustn't walk between the panels.

exercicios.enunciado: Kofi's company uses water to clean the panels. In your opinion, is that a problem? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Yes, I think it's a problem, because water is expensive in dry places, and people need it for drinking. A machine without water is a better solution, even if it costs more at the start.

Visitors are coming to your workplace or your school. Give them a short safety briefing: at least four steps or rules, with sequence words.
exercicios.frase: First
exercicios.resposta: Welcome! First, you sign in at reception and get a visitor card. You have to wear it all the time. Then I'll show you the emergency exits. You mustn't use the lift in a fire. If you hear the alarm, go to the assembly point in the car park. Finally, you don't have to wear special clothes.

exercicios.enunciado: A foreign visitor asks about this sign. Explain it in English: "Laboratório — É obrigatório o uso de óculos de protecção. Proibido comer e beber. Em caso de derrame de produtos químicos, avise imediatamente o técnico responsável."
exercicios.frase: It says
exercicios.resposta: It says this is a lab. You have to wear safety glasses. You mustn't eat or drink here. And if you spill a chemical, you have to tell the technician who's responsible — immediately.

Explain a process or a procedure at your work, or in your studies. Use sequence words and at least two passive sentences.
exercicios.frase: First
exercicios.resposta: In our warehouse, an order is prepared in five steps. First, it's received by email. Then it's checked by the manager. After that, the products are taken from the shelves and put in boxes. Once the boxes are ready, they're sent by lorry. Finally, the client gets a message.

exercicios.enunciado: Describe a place you know well: who works there, what is done there, and one rule.
exercicios.frase: where
exercicios.resposta: The library where I study is in the centre of the city. The librarians who work there are very helpful. Books are lent for two weeks, and you mustn't eat inside.
